title: Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act, Public Law 117-78 (135 Stat. 1525)
notes: Statute. Sec. 3(a) presumption for goods 'wholly or in part' from XUAR or listed entities; Sec. 3(b) exception requires full compliance with guidance + clear and convincing evidence; Sec. 2(d)(2)(B)(viii) mandates cotton, tomatoes, polysilicon as high-priority sectors.

title: The Department of Homeland Security Issues Withhold Release Order on Silica-Based Products Made by Forced Labor in Xinjiang
notes: Hoshine WRO; applies to Hoshine and its subsidiaries and to goods derived from its silica-based products (e.g., polysilicon). Notes June 2021 DOL listing of Xinjiang polysilicon and BIS licence requirements on Xinjiang polysilicon producers.

title: Strategy to Prevent the Importation of Goods Mined, Produced, or Manufactured with Forced Labor in the People's Republic of China (UFLPA Strategy)
publisher: DHS / Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force
notes: Initial 20-entity list sourced from existing CBP WROs and BIS Entity List; importer guidance on tracing 'from raw materials to finished good'; summarises 180 public comments and April 8 2022 hearing.

title: UFLPA Operational Guidance for Importers (CBP Pub. 1793-0522)
notes: Polysilicon annex: flow chart from location of quartzite to polysilicon to downstream facilities; warns factories sourcing both XUAR and non-XUAR polysilicon risk detention. Superseded June 2026 by EV-013.

title: 2023 Updates to the Strategy to Prevent the Importation of Goods Mined, Produced, or Manufactured with Forced Labor in the PRC
notes: CBP risk-based targeting prioritises direct XUAR imports, listed entities, third-country manufacturing/transshipment, and non-XUAR entities related (parent/subsidiary/affiliate) to XUAR entities that are also likely to contain XUAR inputs.

title: 2024 Updates to the Strategy to Prevent the Importation of Goods Mined, Produced, or Manufactured with Forced Labor in the PRC
notes: List grew 20 -> 68; FLETF 'prioritized its efforts to identify entities who have egregiously, and with corroborated evidence' met criteria; improved, 'scalable' listing process; added PVC, aluminum, seafood sectors.

title: 2025 Updates to the Strategy to Prevent the Importation of Goods Mined, Produced, or Manufactured with Forced Labor in the PRC
notes: Adds caustic soda, copper, lithium, red dates, steel as high-priority sectors; list at 144; DHS page states >16,700 shipments reviewed (~$3.7bn). No 2026 update located (see open questions).

title: UFLPA Frequently Asked Questions
notes: Living page (accessed date governs). From May 16 2024 FLETF counts named subsidiaries/affiliates individually (+9 entities). Presumption covers goods made elsewhere that incorporate XUAR or listed-entity inputs. Removal process via FLETF Chair.

title: FAQs: Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) Enforcement
notes: Living page. Summary tracing report for supply chains identical to one previously cleared cuts detention to avg 10-14 days; same applies to commingled supply chains.

title: CSMS # 63743803 - DHS Places New Additions to UFLPA Entity List
publisher: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CSMS bulletin)
notes: 37 additions effective 2025-01-15 (total 144) incl. Donghai JA Solar Technology (Jiangsu; sources polysilicon from XUAR producer), Hongyuan Green Energy + subsidiary (Inner Mongolia), Shuangliang Silicon; Zijin Mining + Xinjiang subsidiaries.

title: Notice Regarding the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List (FR Doc. 2026-15628, 91 FR 48913)
notes: Supersedes the Jan 15 2025 list; adds 43 (total 187). TBEA listed under 2(d)(2)(B)(v) for sourcing aluminum (and Tianchi Energy coal) from XUAR; technical correction renames Xinjiang GCL to Xinjiang Goens Energy Technology (polysilicon). Tianshan Aluminum listed with seven named subsidiaries.

title: Notice Regarding the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List (FR Doc. 2026-22094)
notes: Adds BGI Genomics, MGI Tech, Shenzhen BGI Technology (total 190). Non-solar; used for timeline/trigger-scope trend only.

title: CBP Forced Labor Enforcement Operational Guidance for Importers (CBP Pub. 5560-0526)
notes: Consolidates UFLPA, Sec. 307 and CAATSA guidance; supersedes June 2022 guidance. Silica-based products annex keeps quartzite-to-import flow chart and commingling warning. Release date per CBP document page.

title: Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) Enforcement Statistics Dashboard Guide
notes: Defines 'shipment' as individual import transaction; 'stopped' = automated hold, not necessarily physical detention. Example: 65,707 stopped shipments ($3.91bn) through 2025-11-24. Solar sector referenced via HTS 8541.

title: Forced Labor Imports: DHS Increased Resources and Enforcement Efforts, but Needs to Improve Workforce Planning and Monitoring (GAO-21-106)
notes: Pre-UFLPA capacity baseline: Forced Labor Division spending ~$1m (FY18) to $1.4m (FY19); staff shortage suspended some investigations; CBP reported completing workforce assessment by March 2023. No UFLPA-specific GAO report located.

title: U.S. Customs and Border Protection Budget Overview, Fiscal Year 2025 Congressional Justification
notes: FY2022-23 appropriations supported hiring 338 positions CBP-wide for UFLPA/forced labor; FY2025 request +$19.9m to sustain 336 FTE and tracing technology.

title: Joint Explanatory Statement, Division C - Department of Homeland Security Appropriations (FY2026)
notes: Directs CBP to allocate not less than FY2025 levels to forced-labor enforcement and to brief on UFLPA implementation incl. transshipment of XUAR-related goods.

title: Letter from Reps. DeLauro, Krishnamoorthi et al. to DHS and CBP on UFLPA enforcement
publisher: Office of Rep. Rosa DeLauro (U.S. House)
notes: Democratic members' oversight letter. Cites CBP data: avg 1,062 stopped shipments/month Nov 2024-Mar 2025 vs 224/month Apr-Aug 2025; zero list additions since 2025-01-15; asks whether resources diverted to tariffs and about cuts at TIP/DRL/ILAB.

title: Select Committee on China and CECC Back DHS's Enforcement of UFLPA (letter requesting briefing)
publisher: House Select Committee on the CCP
notes: Bipartisan (Moolenaar, Khanna, Smith, Merkley, McGovern, Thompson et al.). Requests briefing on priorities incl. polysilicon, barriers/resource constraints to listing, evidentiary standards, staffing changes since 2024. Date approx. (InsideTrade report dated 2026-09-03).

title: One Year Suspension of Expansion of End-User Controls for Affiliates of Certain Listed Entities (FR Doc. 2025-19846)
publisher: Bureau of Industry and Security, Dept. of Commerce (Federal Register)
notes: BIS (not UFLPA) Affiliates Rule of 2025-09-30 applied Entity List restrictions to >=50%-owned affiliates; suspended 2025-11-10 to 2026-11-09, scheduled to resume 2026-11-10. Comparator for the ownership_reach dial.

title: Camel Group Co., Ltd. v. United States, Slip Op. 26-95 (Ct. Int'l Trade)
notes: APA review of FLETF refusal to remove Camel Group (listed 2023-08-02); remanded for lack of reasoned decision-making, without vacatur; cites Ninestar II. Published in Customs Bulletin Vol. 60 No. 26 (2026-09-02); exact opinion date not captured.

title: DHS Announces the Addition of 43 Companies to the UFLPA Entity List
notes: Press release: 187 entities, '30% increase', 'single largest-ever expansion'; sectors aluminum, apparel, copper, cotton, tomatoes; frames additions as protecting American businesses from unfair competition.

title: Comment Submitted by Solar Energy Industries Association (DHS-2022-0001-0128), 'SEIA UFLPA Comments 3.10.2022'
publisher: Solar Energy Industries Association via Regulations.gov
notes: Trade association comment to FLETF docket. Recommends public-private partnership, recognition of verified importers (traceability programme with third-party audit), pre-detention procedures (CF-28 / RASA) before detention. Reliable for what was said, not for truth of claims.

title: Comment Submitted by American Clean Power Association (DHS-2022-0001-0163), 'ACP - UFLPA Comments AS FILED'
publisher: American Clean Power Association via Regulations.gov
notes: Describes Hoshine WRO detentions from Aug 2021 affecting suppliers of ~two-thirds of US modules; asks that a source shown XUAR-free not be re-examined across detentions and that detentions not rest on outdated information.

title: Comment Submitted by First Solar, Inc. (DHS-2022-0001-0175), 'Public Comments on UFLPA Enforcement'
notes: US thin-film maker (no polysilicon) with commercial interest in strict enforcement. Urges scrutiny of makers with long-term supply agreements with XUAR polysilicon producers or producers with XUAR subsidiaries, and ties to BIS-listed entities; notes polysilicon blending and multiple BOMs hamper traceability.

title: First Solar, Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal year ended 2025-12-31
notes: Risk factors / business: does not use polysilicon, mitigating UFLPA disruption; main competitors are crystalline-silicon makers 'the majority of which are linked to China'; competes on responsible sourcing.

title: Maxeon Solar Technologies Form 20-F for fiscal year 2024
notes: Discloses UFLPA detentions of US imports since July 2024; revenue decline of $614.1m attributed primarily to detentions; CBP denied protests late March 2025; CIT action filed. Describes Hoshine-era 'lengthy and arduous process' of proving no forced labor 'at the furthest upstream stages'.

title: In Broad Daylight: Uyghur Forced Labour and Global Solar Supply Chains
publisher: Sheffield Hallam University, Helena Kennedy Centre (Murphy & Elima)
notes: XUAR ~45% of 2020 solar-grade polysilicon; traces quartz to module; names Hoshine, Daqo, GCL, TBEA/Xinte, East Hope; argues manufacturers must scrutinise down to raw quartz because MGS and polysilicon are blended.

title: Over-Exposed: Uyghur Region Exposure Assessment for Solar Industry Sourcing
notes: Published July 2023, updated Nov 2023. XUAR ~35% of 2022 polysilicon, up to 32% of global MGS; finds bifurcated supply chains; argues industry treated polysilicon as a 'raw material', overlooking quartz/MGS tiers.

title: Section 307 and Imports Produced by Forced Labor (IF11360)
notes: CRS (nonpartisan, congressional). As of March 2026 ~42,000 shipments detained ($3.9bn); list grew 20 -> nearly 150; notes Dec 2025 members' letter on 2025 decline; cites 2020 GAO staff-shortage finding and later funding increases.

title: Allies seek to follow U.S. lead on Xinjiang forced labor ban - U.S. official
notes: Reports lawmakers asked CBP why three major Chinese solar companies were excluded from the list; notes expansion could threaten solar supply and decarbonisation goals; DOL's Thea Lee: 'competing objectives within an administration'. Underlying letter not located.

title: Exclusive: U.S. blocks more than 1,000 solar shipments over Chinese slave labor concerns
notes: CBP public-records response: 1,053 solar shipments detained 2022-06-21 to 2022-10-25, none released; ACP: Q3 installs -23%, ~23 GW delayed; CBP: timing 'contingent upon how quickly an importer is able to submit sufficient documentation'.

title: Exclusive: U.S. solar panel imports from China grow, alleviating gridlock, officials say
notes: John Podesta (CERAWeek): 'clearer guidance out'; Trina: >900 MW cleared in four months, <1% detained; CBP had released 374 of 1,433 electronics shipments. Date month-level (CERAWeek week).

title: Solar dominates import seizures after US ban on Chinese forced labor goods
notes: New CBP HTS breakdown: HTS 8541 (incl. solar) $3.26bn of $3.94bn stopped (82%); >79% of that value released; stopped value 2025 $187.7m vs $1.78bn 2024; most from Malaysia, Vietnam, Thailand.

title: What's Next for the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act?
publisher: Center for Strategic and International Studies
notes: Q3 2022: >1,500 stops, >1,000 electronics (mostly solar), 69% from Malaysia/Vietnam; DHS under pressure to expand list; stopping all research-named categories 'an impossible task for CBP' even with added resources. Exact date not captured.

title: Assessing the Impact of the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act After Three Years
publisher: Center for Strategic and International Studies
notes: Citing Bernreuter: XUAR polysilicon share ~41% -> 24.8% by capacity since 2021; XUAR share of China MGS rose to 53%; separate US-bound lines. Notes no new entities and falling detentions in 2025; 'political will is critical'. Data to Aug 2025.

title: Forced Labor in Global Supply Chains: Trade Enforcement (RR-A2534-1)
notes: Using FactSet relationship data: US businesses with 2nd-4th tier links to XUAR entities persisting or growing since UFLPA; share of shipments from XUAR-connected global firms roughly constant. Authors caution apparent increase may reflect better data.

title: Experts: UFLPA Enforcement Changing as CBP Tested by Tariffs Changes
notes: Luke Tillman (ex-CBP attorney, now LONGi general counsel - interested party): Electronics CEE stopped granting extensions in 2025; 'loss of talent at CBP'; resources 'stretched'; early-2024 questionnaire to solar importers 'best enforcement tool'.

title: ArentFox Schiff 2026 Forced Labor Guide for Global Businesses
notes: Law-firm analysis: HTS 8541 >61% of FY2025 stopped value; solar focus driven partly by 2024 questionnaires to large importers; from April 2025 CBP sometimes excluded goods immediately, bypassing detention; refers to 'tariff-driven distractions of 2025'.

title: DHS Adds Three Chinese Companies to UFLPA Entity List as China Threatens Retaliation
notes: Reports MOFCOM on 2026-08-05 put six US organisations (Altana, Responsible Business Alliance, Verite, Stratum Reservoir, Applied DNA Sciences, Human Rights in China) on its countermeasures list over Xinjiang listings; removal petitions not appealable, no decision timeline.

title: ANSI Approves New SEIA Standard to Enhance Solar Supply Chain Transparency
notes: ANSI/SEIA 101 traces origins 'from raw materials to finished goods', built on examples of shipments detained and released by CBP. Exact date not captured (listed near Oct 2025 releases).

title: Coalition Urges Robust Enforcement Four Years After UFLPA Implementation
publisher: Coalition to End Forced Labour in the Uyghur Region
notes: Advocacy: dashboard shows decline; no list additions since 2025-01-15; 'static list' forecloses use of presumption (Corporate Accountability Lab). Date approx. (four-year anniversary).

title: China: US Law Against Uyghur Forced Labor Takes Effect
notes: Advocacy: 'clear and convincing evidence' is 'a near impossible bar' for XUAR sourcing because surveillance and threats prevent meaningful audits; urges no audits/certifications in Xinjiang.
